transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-31
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 52 mins
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Lena (Apogee VP Eng), Marco (Apogee SRE), Aisha (Apogee Security), Tommy (Apogee Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): kickoff; high-level network + security; pilot scoping for chat & embeddings; runbook / perf tests; next steps assigned.

[00:00:05] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer and Evan who's the CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:14] Lena Park: Good thanks. Excited to get started. We just want to make sure this pilot is low friction — security and cost are big for us.
[00:00:23] Priya Sood: Totally. We'll try to make the first two weeks very prescriptive. Today we'll align on network, SSO/KMS, and scope.
[00:00:35] Marco Ruiz: Short context — we run microservices on k8s in GCP. We use private services access, and prefer not to punch public egress for inference.
[00:00:47] Priya Sood: Got it. For Redwood Dedicated we support VPC peering or Private Link type setups — I might say privatelink but some transcripts call it private link or private-link. Either way you can keep traffic in your network.
[00:00:59] Aisha Khan: On the security side we need SOC2 docs, encryption in transit at TLS 1.2+, and KMS integration. We also have to know about key custody — do you let us bring our KMS?
[00:01:13] Jordan Miles: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. There are some limits depending on on-prem vs hosted, but for Dedicated you can bring keys — Priya can share the KMS checklist.
[00:01:25] Priya Sood: I'll post the KMS integration notes. Note: there are a couple of steps — key policies, granting Redwood service principal access, and verifying via test envelopes.
[00:01:39] Tommy Chen: Also about traffic — short bursts vs steady QPS — our expected load is 10 qps for chat during peak, and embeddings backfill of ~50k vectors over a week. We want to estimate cost and latency.
[00:01:53] Priya Sood: Helpful. For cost and perf we'll run a baseline with small and long sequence tests so latency and throughput numbers line up with your burst profile.
[00:02:06] Marco Ruiz: Are there recommended quantization settings? We care about quality but will trade for cost if needed.
[00:02:12] Priya Sood: Yes — we have quant profiles per model; for chat we'd typically start with int8 or 4-bit depending on model. We'll recommend after we see your eval prompts. Sometimes the quant names get munged in notes — like Q-8 or 4bit — but we'll be explicit in the runbook.
[00:02:30] Lena Park: Timeline — we want pilot running in staging in two weeks. Is that realistic?
[00:02:36] Evan Li: Two weeks is doable if networking and access are ready this week. The critical path is VPC peering + service account permissions + allowlist.
[00:02:47] Jordan Miles: I'll send a staging access doc and a VPC checklist by Friday. That's the onboarding runbook excerpt.
[00:02:55] Aisha Khan: We'll need to review the audit log retention and where logs are stored. Also can we get attestation for crypto modules?
[00:03:04] Priya Sood: Audit logs are available with Dedicated, and we can configure retention windows; for crypto attestation we'll share the HSM/KMS whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts.
[00:03:15] Marco Ruiz: Small note — our infra team uses DataDog for tracing. Any tracing hooks?
[00:03:21] Priya Sood: Yes we expose tracing headers and can integrate with DataDog via our tracing API; we'll set up an example in the runbook.
[00:03:31] Lena Park: Good. Onboarding items — who owns what on Redwood side?
[00:03:35] Jordan Miles: Jordan for runbook / access doc, Priya for perf testing and technical setup, Evan will coordinate the go/no-go and success criteria.
[00:03:45] Lena Park: On our side, Tommy will handle cloud networking, Marco will handle load tests and instrumentation, and Aisha handles security review.
[00:03:55] Jordan Miles: Let's walk through the pilot scope: Week 0 — staging access and networking; Week 1 — deploy test harness, run perf baselines and initial evals; Week 2 — iterate on quantization and cost tuning, validate success criteria and handoff plan.
[00:04:12] Marco Ruiz: For the perf baseline — can you run small seq (128 tokens) and long seq (1024 tokens) both for chat? Also embeddings batch throughput for 512-d vectors — we'll provide vector dims.
[00:04:27] Priya Sood: Yep. We'll run tests and share CSVs with p95/p99 latency, throughput and token/cost estimates. Note: sometimes the transcript autosub replaces p95 with p9-five — ignore that.
[00:04:40] Aisha Khan: On SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for users. Does Redwood support SAML + SCIM?
[00:04:47] Jordan Miles: Yes, SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; we'll include the SAML metadata file and SCIM endpoint details in the runbook.
[00:04:58] Lena Park: Any blockers we should flag up-front?
[00:05:01] Priya Sood: Biggest are network peering delays (sometimes infra ticket queues add a week), and KMS policy approvals. If infra can allowlist our IPs this week we can be green.
[00:05:13] Tommy Chen: We can do the allowlist today and open a ticket with our cloud provider.
[00:05:18] Marco Ruiz: Also clarify data retention — embeddings retention vs logs — we have regulatory constraints for a subset of PII.
[00:05:26] Evan Li: We'll capture retention policy options in the security appendix. For PII-sensitive traffic, we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed keys and limited retention.
[00:05:38] Aisha Khan: Can you point to an example runbook or shared template?
[00:05:42] Jordan Miles: Yes — I'll share a link to the onboarding runbook and the staging checklist in the follow-up email. (link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/apogee-onboard — placeholder)
[00:05:55] Priya Sood: Quick tech note — your team mentioned k8s; we have a lightweight sidecar example for instrumentation, but for Dedicated most customers prefer direct API calls from their services to avoid additional pods. We'll include both patterns.
[00:06:10] Marco Ruiz: Good to know.
[00:06:12] Lena Park: Ok let's do a quick recap and owners.
[00:06:16] Jordan Miles: Recap: Jordan to send runbook + VPC checklist; Priya to run perf baseline and send results; Evan coordinate go/no-go; Customer: Lena/Tommy/Marco/Aisha to provide traffic + allowlist + security feedback.
[00:06:30] Lena Park: Sounds good.
[00:06:33] Tommy Chen: One more question — if we need a private on-prem option later, is that part of roadmap?
[00:06:39] Jordan Miles: We support a Private deployment option for regulated customers; that's a separate engagement but we'll surface it in the runbook as an FYI.
[00:06:48] Aisha Khan: Great. We'll review and get back within the week.
[00:06:52] Jordan Miles: Awesome — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook and schedule the perf window.
[00:07:00] --- (meeting continues with some screen-share and doc review; timestamps sparse) ---
[00:15:12] Priya Sood: (screen share) here's the VPC checklist: route table entries, firewall rules, DNS entries. I see a question in chat about cross-region latency — we recommend colocating in the same region to reduce hop latency.
[00:26:40] Marco Ruiz: Noted — we'll try to keep staging in the same region.
[00:34:22] Priya Sood: Perf test plan: we'll run 5-minute steady-state tests and 30-second burst tests; collect latency percentiles and token cost per 1k tokens.
[00:41:05] Lena Park: Thanks Priya.
[00:50:12] Jordan Miles: Final note — I'll add a short checklist for legal/procurement (SLA, data processing addendum) and loop in our contracts team if needed.
[00:50:28] Aisha Khan: Please include DPA and any subprocessor list.
[00:50:36] Jordan Miles: Will do.

Meeting end.
